records.title: Creative brief, not tag soup
records.guidance: Anchor the asset's purpose and audience, then describe subject, physical action, environment, composition, visual direction, and output as connected natural language.
records.prompt_shape: Create a [asset] for [purpose/audience]. Show [subject] [action] in [environment], composed as [layout/viewpoint], with [style, light, palette]. [output].

records.title: Canvas and layout first
records.guidance: When structure matters, declare orientation, aspect ratio, grid or fixed regions, and subject placement before surface detail so the model budgets space correctly.
records.prompt_shape: Design a [ratio/orientation] [asset] with [named regions/grid]. Place [subject] in [position] and reserve [negative-space zone] for [purpose].
pitfalls: Adding ratio only after a dense scene description

records.title: Exact visible text contract
records.guidance: Quote every literal string and specify language, position, font character, size hierarchy, alignment, and readability. Preserve user spelling, accents, punctuation, and case. Fill every information slot with real copy instead of placeholders, say how many times each string should appear, and keep any numbers internally consistent so the model does not correct them for you. Dense layouts benefit from an explicit crisp, correctly spelled constraint.
records.prompt_shape: Exact readable text: headline "[TEXT]" at [position] in [type style and size], rendered exactly once; subtitle "[TEXT]" at [position] in [smaller style]. Every line of type crisp and correctly spelled, no extra characters.
pitfalls: Placeholder copy left in a slot

records.title: Concrete scene density
records.guidance: Use 5-12 concrete scene nouns and explicit spatial relationships. Add a few material and lighting controls instead of stacking vague praise words.
records.prompt_shape: [Subject] at [location], surrounded by [specific props and surfaces], with [foreground], [midground], and [background relationship].

records.title: Single capture context for realism
records.guidance: Choose one dominant capture context—device or camera feel, viewpoint, focal length, exposure character, and ordinary imperfections—to make realism observable. Read lens and framing language as visual direction rather than an exact optical simulation, and keep every camera detail inside that one context.
records.prompt_shape: [Editorial/candid/documentary] photograph captured [viewpoint] with [one camera/lens context], [light source], [ordinary imperfections].
pitfalls: Expecting exact optical simulation from lens metadata

records.title: Separate material, lighting, and palette
records.guidance: Control surfaces, light, and color as three independent systems. Describe texture and physical response, light source/direction/softness, then dominant and accent colors.
records.prompt_shape: Materials: [surfaces/textures]. Lighting: [source, direction, softness, temperature, shadow]. Palette: [dominants, accent, saturation/value].

records.title: Targeted avoid constraints
records.guidance: Use a short avoid line only for likely model defaults or defects, while positively describing the intended result. A short avoid list suits GPT Image 2.5; for Gemini and Nano Banana prefer positive framing such as empty street instead of no cars. Prioritize identity drift, geometry, text, edge, and style conflicts relevant to the task.
records.prompt_shape: Avoid [3-6 concrete failure modes]; keep [positive target behavior].

records.title: Multi-panel consistency contract
records.guidance: State exact panel count and grid, assign each panel a role, and lock shared identity, proportions, costume, palette, medium, and environment motifs across the set. A hero-plus-details collage (one large panel plus smaller supporting views) also works when the layout is named and every panel gets its content. For a recurring character, introduce it once on a plain backdrop, then repeat its defining details in every later scene and forbid redesign.
records.prompt_shape: Create a [rows × columns] board. Panel 1: [...]. Panel 2: [...]. Keep [shared constraints] identical across every panel.
pitfalls: Repeating defining details only in the first image of a series
Letting a redesign request pass without an explicit do-not-redesign line

records.title: Change one element, keep the inventory
records.guidance: Name the single element that changes, list the inventory that must survive (surrounding objects, surfaces, framing, background, light direction), and name the physical consequences the model should rebuild such as contact shadow, reflection, and occlusion. State exclusions for unwanted text, logos, and watermarks, and restate the invariants on every turn instead of assuming an earlier turn is remembered. When a region must stay pixel-identical, composite the approved edit back into the original instead of relying on the prompt.
records.prompt_shape: Change only [single element]: [desired result]. Keep everything else exactly as it is: [inventory of objects, surfaces, framing, background, light direction]. Rebuild [contact shadow, reflection, occlusion]. Do not add [text, logos, watermarks] and do not restyle the scene.
pitfalls: Preserve list omitted, so the scene gets repainted
Stale shadow or reflection left under the changed element
Assuming a previous turn is remembered
Expecting a pixel-identical region from prompting alone

records.title: Style artefacts, not style names
records.guidance: Naming a style alone tends to return a filter. Name the medium and the artefacts that prove it: misregistration on a color plate, paper tooth, ink mottling, halftone shading, grain, halation, gate weave, uniform blueprint stroke weights without perspective, or a bokashi gradient and keyblock outlines.
records.prompt_shape: [Medium and substrate], with [artefact list: plate misregistration, paper tooth, ink mottling, halftone, grain, halation, gate weave], [line and shading behavior], no gradients unless the medium has them.
pitfalls: Style name with no artefact evidence

records.title: Realistic photography
records.guidance: Define the publication or use context, one capture frame, subject behavior, time/place, natural imperfections, light direction, focus target, texture realism, and crop. Name one known lighting setup (three-point key/fill/rim, or one practical source) instead of "good lighting", and request the textures that read as real: skin with visible pores, wool weave, brushed metal.
records.prompt_shape: A [use-context] photograph of [subject/action] at [place/time], captured [viewpoint and one optics context], lit by [source], with [ordinary imperfections], [ratio].

records.title: Fashion editorial and lookbook
records.guidance: Specify adult subject, garment silhouette and fabric behavior, pose, editorial location, composition, one optics context, skin and fabric micro-texture, and publication ratio.
records.prompt_shape: Full-body editorial fashion photograph for [publication/campaign]. [Adult subject] wears [garment silhouette/material], posing [action] in [location]. [composition, light, optics, palette], [ratio].
pitfalls: Fabric with no gravity or folds

records.title: Product and commerce hero visual
records.guidance: Lock product geometry and label details, then specify surface, background, material response, lighting rig, hero hierarchy, and output crop. Name the material, not the category: navy blue tweed rather than a suit jacket, etched silver leaf rather than armor, glazed ceramic rather than a mug. JSON-like sections work well for complex renders.
records.prompt_shape: Create a [ratio] commercial hero visual. Product: [geometry/material/label]. Environment: [surface/background]. Lighting: [rig]. Composition: [hero placement]. Preserve [brand invariants].

records.title: Food and beverage photography
records.guidance: Describe ingredient state, temperature cues, moisture, texture, serving vessel, motion if any, surface, light, and appetite-focused composition.
records.prompt_shape: A [commercial/editorial] food photograph of [dish/drink], showing [texture, steam/condensation, ingredients, motion], arranged [composition] on [surface], lit by [source].

records.title: Poster, cover, and typography system
records.guidance: Allocate headline, subject, support copy, CTA, and fine-print zones; quote every string and define a clear promotional hierarchy readable at the target distance.
records.prompt_shape: Design a [ratio] [poster/cover]. Headline "[TEXT]" in [style] at [position]; support copy "[TEXT]"; [subject scene]. Maintain [hierarchy, palette, margins].

records.title: Infographic and field guide
records.guidance: Define 3-5 fixed modules, reading order, labels, annotations, legend, and visual hierarchy before illustration detail. Calibrate the depth of the content to a named audience ("suitable for a high-school science textbook"), and have every arrow carry a relationship rather than decoration. Keep copy short and verify factual content.
records.prompt_shape: Create a [ratio] [field guide/infographic] with [named modules]. Use [arrows/callouts/icons] to show [relationships], exact labels [...], and a [legend/footer].
pitfalls: Depth that does not match the stated audience

records.title: Research and technical diagram
records.guidance: Use diagram grammar: panels, nodes, zones, arrows, line semantics, exact module labels, legend, and publication constraints. Separate facts from illustrative placeholders.
records.prompt_shape: Landscape [venue/style] figure with [columns/zones]. Show [nodes/modules] connected by [directed relationships]. Encode [meaning] with [color/line/thickness]. Exact labels: [...].

records.title: Data visualization
records.guidance: Name the chart family, data and units, encoding rules, scales, labels, legend, and annotation logic. Keep repeated panels aligned and accessible.
records.prompt_shape: Create a [chart family] showing [data]. X-axis [...], Y-axis [...], units [...]. Encode [variable] by [color/size/thickness]. Include [legend, annotations, source note].

records.title: UI and UX mockup
records.guidance: Write the prompt like a product spec: fictional product, device/canvas, information architecture, components, real copy/data, states, palette, spacing, and precise alignment.
records.prompt_shape: Create a high-fidelity [platform/device] screen for [fictional product]. Canvas [...]. Header [...]. Components [...]. Navigation [...]. Exact copy/data [...].

records.title: Brand identity presentation board
records.guidance: Show an original mark and wordmark with palette, type system, spacing behavior, packaging, social or physical touchpoints, and one coherent board hierarchy.
records.prompt_shape: Create a [ratio] brand identity board for fictional [brand]. Include [mark, wordmark, palette, type, packaging, touchpoints] arranged in [grid].

records.title: Architecture and interior
records.guidance: Specify room/building type, viewpoint, spatial layout, materials, light direction, human scale, negative space, and realistic contact shadows.
records.prompt_shape: [Viewpoint] architectural image of [space], organized as [spatial layout], using [materials], lit from [direction/source], with [human-scale cues and negative space].

records.title: Character design sheet
records.guidance: Lock original identity and proportions, then request exact front/side/back views, expressions, outfit or parts breakdown, palette, scale, and shared rendering treatment.
records.prompt_shape: Create a [grid] character design sheet for original [character]. Include [front/side/back], [expressions], [parts/outfit], and [palette], all with identical identity and proportions.

records.title: Storyboard and cinematic sequence
records.guidance: State grid and panel order, assign each panel a story beat, shot size, viewpoint, movement cue, duration, and continuity constraints.
records.prompt_shape: Create a [grid] storyboard for [sequence]. Panel 1: [shot/beat]. Panel 2: [...]. Keep [character, costume, palette, environment] consistent.

records.title: Illustration and fine-art direction
records.guidance: Choose a bounded medium and production context, then define line or brush behavior, shape language, paper/canvas texture, palette, scene density, and finish. Keep reusable characters and products original.
records.prompt_shape: An original [publication/artifact] illustration of [subject/action] in [environment], made with [medium], [line/brush behavior], [texture], and [bounded palette].

records.title: Technical illustration and exploded view
records.guidance: Define exploded or cutaway structure, ordered components, assembly axis, numbered callouts, materials, scale, line style, and plate or blueprint presentation.
records.prompt_shape: Create a [ratio] [exploded/cutaway] technical plate of [object]. Arrange components along [axis/order], label [numbers/names], and show [materials, scale, line semantics].

records.title: Tattoo design and flash sheet
records.guidance: Fix placement and tradition before detail: linework or shading system, color tradition, stencil-ready silhouette, and negative-space gaps that let the design breathe on skin. Present the artwork as a flash sheet or design poster on paper, never rendered on a real body photo.
records.prompt_shape: Create a portrait tattoo [flash sheet/back-piece layout] for [placement]. Subject: [motifs]. Style: [linework and shading tradition, limited palette], with [negative-space gaps] and a stencil-ready silhouette on [paper texture]. Small readable labels: "[STYLE TOKEN]". Make it a professional tattoo design presentation.
pitfalls: Artwork rendered on real skin instead of a design sheet

records.title: Isometric miniature diorama
records.guidance: Lock the isometric angle and grid first, then populate with named buildings, props, and miniature figures, plus ambient occlusion for miniature depth. Open floors as a cutaway when interiors matter and leave breathing room around the floating diorama.
records.prompt_shape: A detailed isometric 3D miniature diorama of [district/scene] with precise 30-degree isometric alignment on a [tile grid]. Include [buildings, props, tiny figures] along [footprint]. [Open the front walls to show interiors]. Soft ambient light from [direction], [palette], subtle ambient occlusion, clean [background] with space around the diorama.
pitfalls: Stairs or floors that cannot connect
Storefront lettering that turns to gibberish

records.title: Cyberpunk and retro-future board
records.guidance: Choose the delivery format first: one cinematic scene, an asymmetric design board with named panels, or a labeled character grid. Fix a tight neon palette, wet reflective surfaces, holographic signage, and original character designs.
records.prompt_shape: Create a [cinematic scene/asymmetric design board/3x3 card grid] titled "[TITLE]". [Name every panel and its beat or character]. Palette: [two or three neon accents] against [wet asphalt or black]. Materials: [glass, chrome, wet cobbles]. Layered reflections, holographic signage, editorial margins, small readable labels.
pitfalls: Every neon color used at once
Panels that repeat the same beat

records.title: Numbered pose and action contact sheet
records.guidance: For motion or video references, lock the character from the supplied reference image, request one grid with an exact cell count and reading order, number every cell, and hold identity, outfit, and accessories constant at a fixed scale on a plain background.
records.prompt_shape: Using reference image 1 as the character design, create a square 4-by-4 contact sheet showing [ACTION SEQUENCE] in 16 distinct full-body poses, read left to right, top to bottom. Number each cell 1-16 in its upper-left corner. Preserve [identity features, outfit, colors, accessories] at consistent scale on a white background. Do not crop limbs. Include no text except the panel numbers.
pitfalls: Identity or accessories changing between cells
Limbs cropped at the frame edge
Treating one sheet as an animation

records.title: Document and publication page
records.guidance: Define page size, column grid, table of contents, figure and caption system, and heading hierarchy before content, then keep tables and captions locked to that grid.
records.prompt_shape: Create a [page size and orientation] [white paper/manual/encyclopedia plate] page about [subject]. Grid: [columns and margins]. Header "[PAGE TITLE]", contents [named sections]. Figures: [type] with captions [...]; table [columns and units]. Typography hierarchy: [headings, body, captions]. Keep charts aligned to the page grid and text readable.
pitfalls: Figures floating off the page grid
Every page element at the same weight

records.title: 3D collectible figure
records.guidance: Carry identity anchors from the reference into a premium collectible: preserve face and outfit first, then specify toy material, base, packaging, studio lighting, and collectible scale.
records.prompt_shape: Turn reference image 1 into a premium 3D collectible figure of [character]. Preserve [face and outfit anchors]. Material: [vinyl/resin finish with toy specular]. Base: [pedestal]. Presentation: [blind-box packaging/desk display] with the minimal accurate label "[LABEL]". Studio lighting, collectible scale.
pitfalls: Generic toy body with no identity anchors
Photoreal skin instead of toy material
Scale that reads as a real person

records.title: Historical and classical theme
records.guidance: Name one period with its clothing system, objects, and layout format, then keep every prop inside that period. Choose scroll, album page, or poster format deliberately instead of defaulting to a poster.
records.prompt_shape: Create a [scroll/album page/poster] in [period] style about [subject]. Clothing and objects: [period-accurate references]. Medium: [ink wash/gongbi/brush] on [paper texture] in [restrained palette]. Layout and reading order: [order]. Keep every prop inside [period]; avoid modern objects.
pitfalls: Modern props inside a period scene
Scroll format with no reading order
Calligraphy that becomes fake glyph clutter

records.title: Sticker sheet and die-cut pack
records.guidance: Treat the pack as a set system: fix the count, the border treatment, the shared illustration style, and the sheet layout, then vary subject per sticker while keeping line weight, palette, and finish identical.
records.prompt_shape: Create a set of [count] die-cut stickers arranged as a sticker sheet on [background]. Shared style: [line weight, palette, rounded shapes, shading], [thick white border or holographic finish], glossy specular highlights, subtle drop shadows. Each sticker: [subject list]. Keep the illustration style identical across the set.
pitfalls: Stickers with inconsistent line weight or palette
Subjects too detailed to read at sticker scale

records.title: Game key art and in-game screenshot
records.guidance: Pick the game-camera context and the display context first, then populate the playable scene and add a restrained HUD with health, stamina, quest text, and minimap. Keep every character, level, and logo original.
records.prompt_shape: Create an original [genre] game [key art/in-game screenshot] in [game-camera context] at [ratio]. Scene: [playable environment, characters, action]. HUD: [health, stamina, quest text, minimap]. Materials and lighting: [...]. Premium next-gen look with believable, readable UI.
pitfalls: Copying an existing game's characters, levels, or logos
Screenshot with no camera or display context

records.title: Photograph of a screen, not a screenshot
records.guidance: Ask for a raw phone photo of a display rather than a screenshot: name the viewpoint and hand-held quality, then add glass and pixel evidence such as the RGB subpixel grid, moiré bands, dust, fingerprints, and uneven reflections.
records.prompt_shape: Create a raw smartphone photo of a [laptop/monitor/phone] screen, not a screenshot, [ratio], [viewpoint] with [device edge and surroundings visible]. Show [visible RGB subpixel grid, subtle moiré bands, dust specks, faint fingerprints, uneven glass reflections, handheld noise, slight perspective skew]. Screen content: [UI description with exact fictional labels].
pitfalls: Result reads as a clean screenshot
No glass, pixel, or reflection evidence

records.title: Text-to-image generation
records.guidance: Describe the complete desired result: purpose, canvas, subject, action, environment, composition, visual direction, text, output, and targeted avoids.
records.prompt_shape: Create [asset/purpose]. [Canvas/layout]. [Subject/action/environment]. [Composition]. [style/material/light/palette]. [text/output/avoid].
pitfalls: Mixing edit language into a fresh generation

records.title: Reference edit with invariants
records.guidance: Lead with the transformation, define the changed target, then explicitly preserve identity, pose, geometry, camera, lighting, background, text, or brand elements that must not drift. Phrase the change as a single condition swap where possible ("make it a winter evening") so the rest of the frame stays put, and preserve a referenced face or identity with several reinforcing signals rather than one: state preservation explicitly, restate the matching features in words, and repeat the invariant at the end.
records.prompt_shape: TASK: [transformation]. CHANGE: [target/result]. PRESERVE: [invariants]. OUTPUT: [crop/fidelity]. AVOID: [task-specific drift].

records.title: Localized inpainting
records.guidance: Name the masked region, desired replacement, local geometry, edge integration, lighting and texture match, then preserve everything outside the region.
records.prompt_shape: Modify only the masked [region]: [change]. Match [adjacent texture, light, perspective]. Preserve every unmasked pixel and the overall composition.

records.title: Multi-reference composition
records.guidance: Identify every image by index and one role, state the base or destination, explain what transfers from each reference, and list invariants for the composed result. For a blend, one sentence per source naming what it contributes, and a bound on how many references are in play, keeps roles from bleeding. If a claim about the reference limit or role count matters, verify the current documented limit for the chosen model.
records.prompt_shape: Image 1 = [base]. Image 2 = [style/garment/object]. Image 3 = [logo/detail]. Apply [specific attribute] from each source to Image 1 while preserving [invariants].

records.title: Reverse prompt from a reference image
records.guidance: Decompose the supplied image into use case, medium, subject type, composition, camera and viewpoint, lighting, color, materials, spatial layers, mood sources, and post-processing, analyzing only dimensions the image actually contains. Promote the 3-5 anchors that most affect similarity into the first third of the prompt.
records.prompt_shape: [3-5 reproduction-critical anchors first: medium boundary, composition, silhouette or pose, signature lighting, key materials, background geometry, color relationships], then [supporting detail: camera and viewpoint, spatial layers, mood through concrete elements, post-processing, target medium]. Avoid [confusable media and likely generation defects].
pitfalls: Inventing brands, people, locations, or camera metadata the image does not show
Style anchors buried after narrative detail
Relying on artist or IP names instead of observable technique

records.title: Gemini and Nano Banana creative brief
records.guidance: Open with a strong verb naming the primary operation, then write connected natural prose: subject, action, location, composition, style, and the output specification at the end. Describe what you want rather than what to exclude, use photographic and cinematic terms to control the camera, and iterate conversationally. For multiple inputs, name each reference and its relationship, then the new scenario.
records.prompt_shape: [Strong verb] a [output type]. [Subject] [action] in [location/context], [composition], [style, light, grade]. [Reference relationship, if any.] [resolution and aspect ratio].
pitfalls: Negative phrasing such as avoid cars instead of empty street
Output spec buried in the middle

records.title: GPT Image 2.5 structured prompt
records.guidance: For GPT Image 2.5, put canvas and layout before subject detail, quote exact text, and drive multi-system visuals (products, food, UI, diagrams, multi-reference edits) with explicit sections or a JSON config block.
records.prompt_shape: CANVAS/LAYOUT: [...]. SUBJECT/SCENE: [...]. MATERIALS/LIGHT/PALETTE: [...]. TEXT: [...]. PRESERVE/AVOID: [...].
pitfalls: Loading every pattern instead of one category

records.title: GPT Image 2.5 model choice and settings
records.guidance: Resolve the model before tuning anything else: Flare trades quality for speed, Sunburst targets quality. Pick a quality level, compare before rewriting the prompt, and raise to xhigh or max only for an unmet requirement inside the latency budget; the same quality label does not imply the same output across models. Compare cost per accepted image rather than per request, and track retry rate, correction turns, and slow-response time alongside visual acceptance when comparing models. Keep model, quality, size, background, and format settings outside the prompt body. For transparent assets request the alpha channel explicitly with PNG or WebP, then check edges. Older models keep their own parameter sets rather than inheriting new ones: the original GPT Image 2 line stops at low/medium/high/auto and always processes inputs at high fidelity, while the earlier 1.x models expose input fidelity and are scheduled for shutdown, so confirm current parameters and deprecation dates before promising a setting.
records.prompt_shape: Prompt: [image brief]. Settings kept outside the prompt: model [flare/sunburst], quality [auto/low/medium/high/xhigh/max], size [ratio/resolution], background [auto/opaque/transparent], input fidelity [low/high, edit only; omit on models that always use high].
pitfalls: Rewriting the prompt when the quality level was the real problem
Assuming a faster model is cheaper per accepted image
Assuming a higher quality setting always improves the result
Expecting a drawn checkerboard to count as transparency
Passing a new model's quality flag to an older model
Building on a model with a shutdown date

records.title: Sketch to realistic render
records.guidance: Split the two jobs: the sketch owns arrangement, the prompt owns finish. Say the drawing is layout guidance only, preserve its proportions, element positions, and perspective, then supply plausible materials, lighting, contact shadows, and environment. Forbid new elements and text unless they are requested.
records.prompt_shape: Turn this drawing into a realistic [photograph/render]. Preserve the exact layout, proportions, and perspective. Choose realistic materials and lighting consistent with the sketch intent: [materials, light, atmosphere]. Do not add new elements or text.
pitfalls: Tracing the sketch literally so it stays a drawing
Creative additions that change the layout
No material or light direction chosen for the model

records.title: Transparent product cutout
records.guidance: Ask for the isolated subject in the prompt and for an alpha background in the settings, forbid the usual intruders (drop shadow, halo, checkerboard, background fill), and name the thin geometry that fails first: cords, wire, hair, perforations, glass edges. Keep PNG without compression for PNG output and re-state the transparency requirement on follow-up edits.
records.prompt_shape: Extract [subject] from the input image and isolate it on a fully transparent background. Output: centered subject, crisp silhouette, clean anti-aliased edges around [thin parts], no halo, no drop shadow, no checkerboard, no background fill. Preserve [geometry and label legibility] exactly and do not restyle the subject.
pitfalls: Asking for transparency only in the prompt or only in the settings
Drop shadow or halo left around the subject
Checkerboard pattern generated as fake transparency
Thin geometry fringed at the edges

records.title: Upscale, restore, and re-render
records.guidance: Separate two jobs that are often mixed: raising resolution and repairing damage. State the target resolution and aspect ratio, then say explicitly that content, composition, and identity must not change; for restoration name the specific repairs (scratches, dust, fading, torn corners) and forbid invented detail, new objects, or restyled faces.
records.prompt_shape: Upscale this image to [resolution] at [aspect ratio]. Preserve composition, geometry, identity, and colors exactly; add no new objects and do not restyle. [For restoration:] repair [scratches, dust, fading, damage] and reconstruct [specific missing areas] faithfully to the original photograph. Keep grain and texture consistent instead of over-smoothing.
pitfalls: Inventing detail that was never in the source
Asking for upscale and restyle in the same pass

records.title: In-image text translation and localization
records.guidance: Localize the copy, not the artwork. Quote every string that changes and its target language, hold layout, typography character, color, and image asset identical, and expect longer target strings to need a smaller size or wider column instead of a re-layout. Re-check that no source-language text survives anywhere in the frame.
records.prompt_shape: Translate all [source language] text in this image into [target language], keeping everything else exactly the same. Replace "[source string]" with "[target string]". Preserve layout, panel geometry, font character, colors, and imagery; adjust only type size or line breaks if the [target language] copy needs more room. Leave no [source language] text.
pitfalls: Re-layouting the whole design instead of the copy
Mixed source and target language left in frame
Longer target strings overflowing their container
Swapping the typeface because the text changed language

records.title: Vibe from signature details, not adjectives
records.guidance: An era or mood lands through ordinary signature objects, not through the label. Replace "nostalgic" with the props and surfaces that produced it: the CD player, beaded curtain, lip glosses, direct flash. Pick two to four era-defining details, and add candid behavior so the scene reads as documentation rather than a styled set.
records.prompt_shape: [Era/style] photograph of [subject] in [setting]. Signature details: [2-4 objects, surfaces, and media of that era]. Light and capture: [era-appropriate flash or available light, grain]. Behavior: [candid action, gaze off camera]. Mood: [evocative pair of words]. Keep the props era-consistent and avoid modern objects.
pitfalls: Naming a decade without any of its objects
Modern props leaking into a period scene
Styled posing instead of candid behavior
Five or more era cues competing for attention

records.title: Physical object mockup of a design
records.guidance: Ask for a photograph of the printed artifact rather than a flat layout. Name the carrier object, its surface and position, the viewing angle, and the print-realism cues that prove it is physical: paper curl, thickness, gloss or matte finish, and the small production marks like issue number, date, barcode, and price.
records.prompt_shape: A photorealistic photograph of [magazine cover/poster/print/box] titled "[TITLE]" [lying on a white shelf/resting against a wall], shot from [angle] with [light]. Show [design content] on the cover, with paper texture, surface reflection, and [small production marks: issue number, date, barcode, price] in the corner. Background: [minimal set]. Text in [typeface character], legible.
pitfalls: Flat layout with no physical carrier or surface
Perfectly flat paper with no curl or thickness
Missing barcode, date, or price on a publication
Perspective that contradicts the described surface

records.title: Role and perspective framing
records.guidance: Ask for an interpretation from a viewpoint instead of a literal scene, then say which signals that viewpoint amplifies so the model does not guess. The prompt supplies the emphasis list; the model supplies the render.
records.prompt_shape: How [role/profession] sees [subject]. Emphasize [signals that viewpoint would foreground, e.g. structure, loads, blueprints, materials, measurements]. [Insert or de-emphasize people and decoration]. Visual language: [drafting, annotations, x-ray, or mixed-media]. [Ratio].
pitfalls: Naming the viewpoint without the signals it emphasizes
Falling back to a plain photo of the subject
